record.original_question: For each prime p and field F, must the p-primary component of the Brauer group satisfy one of the following: it is zero, it contains a nonzero divisible subgroup, or else p = 2 and the 2-primary component is an elementary abelian 2-group?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.6 (Brumer-Rosen [BR68]). For a given field F and each prime p, one of the following holds: (a) (Br F)_p = 0. (b) (Br F)_p contains a nonzero divisible subgroup. (c) p = 2 and (Br F)_2 is an elementary abelian 2-group.

artifact.category_tag: Brauer groups and central simple algebras
artifact.status_search_result: The Brumer–Rosen conjecture on the structure of the p-primary component of the Brauer group of a field (originally posed by Brumer and Rosen in 1968) is listed as an open problem in surveys of central simple algebras, with no general resolution found in the literature. Search results turn up no announced proof or counterexample for arbitrary fields.
